sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: A Discogs release's or master's Tracks view now shows the headings Discogs puts inside a disc ("Cologne 13/02/1981", "Paris 05/02/1981" on a box of live shows) as bands above their tracks, the way Discogs' own page does. Each band says how many tracks it holds and how long they run, and a click folds or shows them; a fold stays through sorting and filtering. On a computer a band stays under the column headers while its tracks scroll past; on a phone or tablet only with the new setting "Tracks view: sticky section bands on touch devices". With a filter on, a band says "2 of 8 tracks", and a section with nothing left loses its band. Sorted by any other column the sections no longer run together, so the bands step aside and each title shows its section as a small tag. The Section column is now hidden by default (it would say the same twice); it is still in 👁️ Visible and the 📊 menu. Mockup: https://claude.ai/artifact/JHuxeos1Yvu7DFwtBftHzg

The Discogs link preview's window shows a release's or master's tracklist as an outline: a shaded bar per disc ("Disc 1 · Volume 1: Live In Europe, 1981 · 13 tracks · 1:16:38") and an indented row per section, each with its tracks and running time, both folding on a click. Chips above the list jump to a disc or a section. Up to about 40 tracks everything starts open; on a bigger release only Disc 1. The card's summary line says how the tracks split: "57 tracks on 5 CDs · 6 sections". Previews already cached are asked from Discogs once more.
